label: nb43-33b-kapitsa
note: Kapitsa's defaults on the MLX 4-bit pack of Nanbeige/Nanbeige4.3-33B @c1093c50 that its catalog ships (`kapitsa pull nanbeige`, kapitsaprime/Nanbeige4.3-33B-MLX-4bit @5901f0d4): every decoder layer in AWQ 4-bit (mlx_lm.awq, affine, group 64), the embedding and LM head in 8-bit, the folder every MLX engine here reads. Plain decoding (no drafter; prompt lookup is off by default). The harness's default sampling (T 0.6, top_p 0.95, top_k 20: Nanbeige's card recommends 0.6 / 0.95 for reasoning and chat). Thinking off through enable_thinking. Its reference prompt tokens (4000: 5088, 16000: 19954) are Nanbeige's chat template rendered by transformers 5.20.2's apply_chat_template, thinking off, and tokenized by tokenizers 0.23.3, the median of 8 nonces (5087-5090, 19953-19957). --slots 1 for parity with the others' single sequence. The SSD prefix cache is a folder in the harness state, emptied before and after each run.

label: nb43-33b-mlxlm
note: mlx-lm's own server on the same weights directory as Kapitsa (its llama model; no drafter). Settings as for the Qwen models: prompt cache for 4 sequences / 8 GB, 2048-token prefill steps (mlx-lm's default). HF_HUB_OFFLINE: mlx_lm.server would otherwise download whatever model a request names. Request id default_model = the model given with --model.

label: nb43-33b-mlxvlm
version_cmd: import importlib.metadata as m; print('mlx-vlm', m.version('mlx-vlm'), 'mlx', m.version('mlx'))
note: mlx-vlm 0.7.10 (MLX_VLM_PYTHON = a Python with it) on the same MLX 4-bit folder, through its own text llama model. Automatic prefix caching on (APC_ENABLED=1, in memory only); 2048-token prefill steps; one sequence at a time. The request's model id is the path the server was started with.

label: nb43-33b-omlx
note: oMLX's plain autoregressive server on the same weights (no drafter exists for this model), with the settings of the Qwen baselines.

label: nb43-33b-llamacpp
model_path: {models}/nanbeige4.3-33b-gguf/Nanbeige4.3-33B-Q4_K_M.gguf (Q4_K_M, converted from the bf16 checkpoint with llama.cpp b11871's convert_hf_to_gguf.py and llama-quantize)
note: Plain llama-server on a Q4_K_M GGUF made from Nanbeige/Nanbeige4.3-33B @c1093c50 with llama.cpp b11871's own tools (convert_hf_to_gguf.py --outtype bf16, llama-quantize Q4_K_M), with two tokenizer metadata fields set false (gguf_set_metadata.py): tokenizer.ggml.add_space_prefix, which as converted puts a U+2581 after every special token, and add_bos_token, which would put a second <|im_start|> before the template's own; with them llama.cpp's tokens of a chat prompt are Hugging Face's. The checkpoint's chat template from a file, with the two minja rewrites Kapitsa's engine makes (llama.cpp's minja parses neither the replace filter nor a method on a macro's result). Flags as the Qwen runs: -c 32768 -np 1, -b/-ub 2048, -lm none, --min-p 0, the harness's sampling. Q4_K_M reads more bytes per token than the MLX 4-bit pack (Q6_K output head and some Q6_K layers), a handicap on bandwidth-bound decode.

label: nb43-33b-ollama
note: Ollama's GGUF runner on the llama.cpp config's Q4_K_M file (its tokenizer metadata fixed as described there), imported with `ollama create nace/nanbeige4.3:33b-q4_K_M` from a Modelfile (Ollama takes the GGUF's own chat template), 32K context, one sequence; thinking off by reasoning_effort none.
